thread.preview:
Good — that one bites *everyone* at least once.

Two quick “future-proof” tips so it doesn’t sneak back in:

- For HUD-only elements (labels, bars, containers), set **Mouse Filter = Ignore** in the Inspector too (so you don’t rely on code order).
- Any full-screen overlay (`ColorRect`, `Panel`, GameOver screen) should be:
  - **Ignore** if gameplay should still receive clicks, or
  - **Stop** if it’s meant to block gameplay (like Game Over), but then you should handle clicks via UI buttons, not player input.

If you want, tell me whether your basic weapon click is handled in `_input` or `_unhandled_input` now, and I’ll suggest the cleanest setup (so UI clicks and gameplay clicks never fight).

content.text: Okay, something got fucked, now, when I click, there isn't any input and nothing happens

items.text:
If **nothing happens on click (and no “LMB -> weapon” print)**, in Godot it’s almost always one of these:

1) the **SceneTree is paused** (so input/processing doesn’t run), or  
2) your **UI is eating the mouse events**, so your `Player._unhandled_input()` never fires.

Here’s the quickest way to fix + confirm which it is.

---

## 1) Hard-reset pause when the game scene loads
Put this at the **top of `game.gd._ready()`**:

```gdscript
func _ready():
	get_tree().paused = false
	print("GAME READY paused=", get_tree().paused)
	# ...rest...
```

If that print shows `paused=true` before you set it, that’s the problem.

---

## 2) Your mouse input is probably being eaten by UI
You’re using `_unhandled_input` in the player. That **only runs if no Control handled the click**. Your HUD (or a full-screen Control/ColorRect) can block it.

### Quick proof (temporary)
In `player.gd`, temporarily change:

```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event):
```

to:

```gdscript
func _input(event):
	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and event.pressed:
		print("PLAYER GOT LMB")
		# your weapon/spell call here
```

If `"PLAYER GOT LMB"` prints now, then the UI *was* swallowing input.

### Proper fix (so UI doesn’t block gameplay clicks)
For any UI nodes that are just display (HUD background, containers, labels), set **Mouse Filter = Ignore**.

Do it in code (fast) in `game.gd._ready()`:

```gdscript
hud.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
for c in hud.get_children():
	if c is Control:
		c.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
```

(Keep actual clickable UI like buttons as default.)

Also, if you ever have a full-screen `ColorRect/Panel` (including your GameOver overlay), that one must be `Ignore` unless it’s intentionally blocking clicks.

---

## 3) One more silent killer: you might be stuck in “GameOver overlay exists but invisible”
If you ever add `GameOverUI` and don’t remove it (or reload), its full-screen `ColorRect` can keep eating clicks.

To be safe, in `GameOverUI.tscn` set the **ColorRect mouse filter to Ignore**:
- Select `ColorRect` → Inspector → **Mouse → Filter → Ignore**

---

### What to send if it still doesn’t work
Paste:
- your `player.gd` input function (whatever handles LMB now)
- your `HUD` scene tree (just node names under HUD)
- confirm if **keyboard movement** works or also dead (that tells me paused vs UI instantly)

But try steps **1 + 2** first — 90% chance it’s one of those.

items.text:
From that log, **your “run ends” logic is firing** (you hit `GAME OVER`). So the missing piece is almost certainly **UI placement/visibility**, plus there’s a *separate* issue causing you to get immediately mulched on respawn.

## A) Why the GameOver UI “doesn’t show”
Right now your `GameOverUI` (a `Control`) is being added under the `Game` (a `Node2D`) or under a `CanvasLayer` that isn’t a `Control`. Anchors/layout behave best when a `Control` is parented to another `Control` that has a real size (like your `HUD`).

### Fix: Add GameOverUI under HUD (not under Game)
In `game.gd`:

```gdscript
func end_run() -> void:
	if _run_ended:
		return
	_run_ended = true

	print("GAME OVER")
	get_tree().paused = true

	_game_over_ui = game_over_ui_scene.instantiate()

	# make sure it works while paused
	_game_over_ui.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_WHEN_PAUSED

	# IMPORTANT: add under a Control that has viewport size
	hud.add_child(_game_over_ui)

	# force full screen just in case
	_game_over_ui.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	_game_over_ui.set_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)

	_game_over_ui.restart_requested.connect(_restart_run)
```

Also remove the duplicate instantiate line you had earlier (you already noticed it).

If you want to be extra-safe visually: set `_game_over_ui.z_index = 999`.

---

## B) You’re dying instantly after respawn (this is in your log)
After you hit 0 HP the first time, you immediately start taking damage again at the spawn HP. That means you’re still “touching enemies” / still in the contact-damage loop when you respawn.

### Fix: clear contact state + give i-frames on respawn
In `player.gd`, in `respawn()` do:

```gdscript
func respawn() -> void:
	# reset contact loop state (important)
	_touching_enemies = 0
	_damage_loop_running = false

	hp = max_hp
	hp_changed.emit(hp, max_hp)
	global_position = spawn_pos
	is_dead = false

	# small invulnerability window
	hurtbox.monitoring = false
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.6).timeout
	hurtbox.monitoring = true
```

That alone stops the “respawn → instantly die again” chain.

---

## C) One more thing: delete `end_run()` from `player.gd`
You have this in player:

```gdscript
func end_run() -> void:
	print("GAME OVER")
	get_tree().paused = true
```

It’s not used, and it can confuse future you. The *only* `end_run()` should live in `game.gd`.

---

If you apply **A + B**, you’ll (1) actually see the Game Over screen reliably and (2) be able to click Restart without instantly getting erased again.

items.text:
Yep — you sent exactly the right bits. Two things jump out that can make “Game Over UI doesn’t show” happen even though the logic *looks* right.

## 1) You’re calling `end_run()` on `current_scene` (fragile)
This line in `player.gd`:

```gdscript
get_tree().current_scene.call_deferred("end_run")
```

works **only if** `current_scene` is the node that actually has `end_run()` (your `Game` root with `game.gd` on it).

As soon as you introduce menus / wrappers / different scene roots, `current_scene` might not be the same node anymore, and then `end_run()` never fires (or you get a “method not found” error somewhere in output).

### Fix (robust): call the parent (since Player is child of Game)
Your scene tree shows `Player` is directly under `Game`, so do:

```gdscript
get_parent().call_deferred("end_run")
```

So your `die()` becomes:

```gdscript
func die() -> void:
	if is_dead:
		return
	is_dead = true

	Global.add_followers(-10)

	if Global.followers > 0:
		respawn()
	else:
		get_parent().call_deferred("end_run")
```

Even better long-term: add Game to a group and find it by group, but parent is perfect for now.

Also: delete `end_run()` from `player.gd` — it’s not used and it can confuse future you.

---

## 2) Your GameOverUI might be added to the wrong “UI layer”
In `game.gd` you do:

```gdscript
add_child(_game_over_ui)
```

`Game` is a `Node2D`. Your GameOverUI is a `Control` using anchors (full screen). Anchors/layout are most reliable when the Control lives under a UI tree (Control/CanvasLayer).

You already have `UI` in the scene. Put the GameOverUI there instead:

```gdscript
$UI.add_child(_game_over_ui)
```

(or `$UI/HUD.add_child(...)` if `$UI` isn’t where you want it visually)

So your `end_run()` should be:

```gdscript
func end_run() -> void:
	if _run_ended:
		return
	_run_ended = true

	print("GAME OVER")
	get_tree().paused = true

	_game_over_ui = game_over_ui_scene.instantiate()
	_game_over_ui.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_WHEN_PAUSED
	$UI.add_child(_game_over_ui)
	_game_over_ui.restart_requested.connect(_restart_run)
```

### Also fix this typo
You instantiate twice right now:

```gdscript
_game_over_ui = game_over_ui_scene.instantiate()
_game_over_ui = game_over_ui_scene.instantiate()
```

Delete one of them.

---

## Quick “prove it” debug line (optional but useful)
Right before calling end_run in `die()`:

```gdscript
print("current_scene=", get_tree().current_scene.name, " parent=", get_parent().name)
```

If you ever see `current_scene` not being `"Game"`, that confirms why `current_scene.call_deferred("end_run")` stopped working.

---

### Minimal changes summary
- **player.gd:** replace `current_scene.call_deferred("end_run")` with `get_parent().call_deferred("end_run")` and remove `player.end_run()`.
- **game.gd:** instantiate once, and add GameOverUI under `$UI` (not under Node2D root).

Do those and your Game Over screen should be back immediately.

items.text:
Send me the **minimum chain that controls “run ends → UI appears”**. In your project that’s basically 4 things:

### 1) `player.gd` (only these functions)
- `die()`
- anything that calls `end_run()` / `call_deferred("end_run")`
- follower loss logic

**Why:** if `end_run()` never gets called, the UI can’t appear.

---

### 2) `game.gd` (full file)
Especially:
- `_ready()` (anything that resets followers / pauses / reloads)
- `end_run()`
- `_restart_run()`

**Why:** game over UI is spawned here.

---

### 3) `GameOverUI.tscn` + `GameOverUI.gd` (if it has a script)
If you can’t paste the whole `.tscn`, at least paste:
- root node type (Control? CanvasLayer?)
- whether it has `process_mode` set
- the signal name you connect (`restart_requested` etc.)

**Why:** if the tree is paused, UI needs to run **when paused** or it won’t respond (and depending on node type/layout it might look like it never appears).

---

### 4) Your `game.tscn` **scene tree screenshot** (or paste the node tree)
I only need the top level, like:

```
Game (Node2D) [script: game.gd]
  Player
  UI
```

**Why:** your `player.gd` calls:
```gdscript
get_tree().current_scene.call_deferred("end_run")
```
If `current_scene` is **not the node that has `end_run()`** (common when you wrap scenes in another root), then nothing happens / you’ll get a “method not found” in debugger.

---

## Most likely causes (so you can sanity-check immediately)
1) **`current_scene` doesn’t have `end_run()` anymore**  
   (e.g. you changed scene structure and `game.gd` is on a child node, not the root)

2) **You pause the tree and the GameOverUI doesn’t process while paused**  
   Fix is:
   ```gdscript
   _game_over_ui.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_WHEN_PAUSED
   ```
   or set it in the GameOverUI scene root inspector.

3) **You’re no longer reaching followers <= 0**  
   So you always respawn, never end the run.

---

If you paste **(1) die() from player.gd + (2) game.gd + (4) the game.tscn node tree**, I can tell you the exact fix in one pass.
